To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Theoretical study of the interactions between a high‐Valent manganese porphirin oxyl‐hydroxo‐Mn(III)‐TMpyP and double‐Stranded DNA.

(i) the oxyl‐(OH)‐MnIV‐TMPyP complex binds to the minor groove of DNA, (ii) the hydroxo ligands of the metallo‐porphyrin are involved in hydrogen bond formation with DNA, and (iii) the hydroxo‐MnIV complex is more reactive than the oxyl‐Manganese(IV) complex toward C5′‐H abstraction from DNA.

The transient oxyl‐( hydroxo)‐Manganese(IV)‐porphyrin derivative, oxyl‐(H2O)‐Mn‐TMPyP (TMPyP is a cationic porphynin) was studied by molecular modeling in order to elucidate the mechanism of interaction of this active species with the minor groove of DNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interactions between a high‐ valent manganese porphirin oxyl‐hydroxo‐Mn(III)‐TpyP and double‐ stranded DNA.
the interaction of the Mn‐TMPyP oxyl‐(hydoroxy)‐MnIV‐porphyrin species with DNA.
the study of the interaction of a high‐valency manganese porphyrins oxyl‐(hydoroxy)‐Mn‐TMPyP with double‐strand DNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mn(IV)‐oxyl‐TMPyP is a good candidate to be the reactive species for DNA cleavage by Mn(III)TMPyP/KPS.
the Mn(IV) porphyrin complex is able to interact with the minor groove of DNA, but the oxyl group is unable to attack the DNA sugar moiety.
the oxyl‐MnP‐TMPyP complex, which is formed by the interaction of Mn(III)TMPyP with KHSO5, is able to interact with DNA, but the interaction is not strong enough to cleave the DNA backbone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new and efficient method of cleaving DNA by using manganese porphyrins as catalysts in conjunction with hydrogen peroxide and a reducing agent, ascorbate.
the DNA‐binding mode of the manganese(IV)‐porphyrin is not significantly affected by the presence of the oxo‐ligand.
the oxyl‐M(IV)‐TMpyP is not able to attack C5′ and C1′ of deoxyribose units of B‐DNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Mn‐TMPyP complex is a good model for understanding the DNA binding properties of the Mn‐TMPyp complex.
the metalloporphyin can interact with the DNA in the minor groove.
the oxyl‐MnPp/DNA system is an efficient DNA‐scission system.
